That typically only happens if the warning message that splitting files with fragment urls with missing targets might cause problems is ignored. The warning message was specifically added because there are certain conditions that can't be properly accommodated by Sigil's splitting routines. Namely: if there is no element with an id of "anchor1" in "this_file.xhtml" the warning will pop. If the warnin g is ignored, paths will not be correctly updated.

If you don't get a warning message in the situations where this can occur, then you might be using an older version of Sigil that doesn't give the warning.

comments.author: kevinhendricks
comments.body:
Updating the ncx after a merge has never been implemented in Sigil.  I will add that to out todo list.  In those instances the user can (re-) generate the toc to correct the ncx.

Yes under epub3, the ncx is never updated.  Since the ncx is optional, the user can generate an ncx from their nav before a final save using a epub3 specific menu item.

So it appears from your test results, the change we made to handle non-spec internal links does not have any bad side effects.

Please note, some browsers treat links with filenames (even the current one) as a need to "load" the page including either cache or network access.  For internal links without a filename, a simple scrollto id is used.  This is true in both Webkit and WebEngine.

So from a performance perspective, not adding a filename for an internal link is a big win.
